Professional Training Delivery Agreement
This agreement records the arrangement between the commissioning organization and
the training provider for the design and delivery of a professional development
programme over 12 months. It sets out the scope of instruction, the schedule of 24
sessions across 12 weeks, the obligations of each party, and the standards by which
satisfactory completion is judged. Both parties confirm they have authority to enter this
arrangement and that the terms below reflect their agreed understanding.

The provider shall design and deliver a structured programme covering the agreed
competency areas, comprising 24 facilitated sessions and 48 teaching hours in total.
Delivery may occur at up to 4 designated sites or through equivalent remote channels
where the parties agree in writing. Any material expansion of subject coverage,
additional cohorts, or supplementary site deployments requires a written variation
signed by both parties before work begins.
Supporting records are presented in Table 3.

A.1 Programme Design and Curriculum
The curriculum shall be built from a documented needs analysis and mapped to the
competency framework supplied by the commissioning organization. Learning outcomes,
session plans, and assessment instruments must be submitted for review before delivery
begins. The provider retains editorial control over instructional method while ensuring
alignment with the agreed outcomes and the professional standards applicable to the
participants' roles.
Supporting records are presented in Table 4.
Table 4: Curriculum design checkpoints and required outputs
A.1.1 Learning Outcomes and Assessment Design
Each module shall state measurable learning outcomes and the evidence that will
demonstrate achievement. Assessment instruments must be valid for the stated
outcomes, applied consistently across cohorts, and moderated by a second qualified
assessor. The provider shall retain assessment records for the period required by the
commissioning organization's policy and make them available on reasonable request.
A.1.1.1 Formative and Summative Components
The programme shall combine formative activities that give participants feedback during
instruction with summative assessments that determine final achievement. Formative
tasks may include structured practice, peer review, and facilitator observation;
summative tasks shall be specified in advance with published criteria. Weighting
between components must be disclosed to participants at the start of each module.
SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT | RESEARCH PROTOTYPE
A.1.1.2 Moderation and Quality Assurance
A moderation process shall verify that assessor judgements are consistent and
defensible. A sample of assessments, proportionate to cohort size and no smaller than
the provider's published standard, shall be independently reviewed. Where moderation
identifies inconsistency, the provider shall adjust results and document the corrective
action taken before issuing final records.
A.1.2 Curriculum Review and Version Control
All curriculum materials shall be version-controlled, with each revision dated and
attributed to an authorized reviewer. The provider shall conduct a scheduled review at
least once during the term and incorporate feedback from participants and the
commissioning organization. Superseded materials must be withdrawn from use so that
participants are not assessed against conflicting criteria.
A.2 Participant Eligibility and Enrolment
The commissioning organization shall nominate participants who meet the stated
prerequisite knowledge and confirm their availability for the scheduled sessions. The
provider shall verify eligibility before enrolment and notify the commissioning
organization of any nominee who does not meet the prerequisites. Substitutions are
permitted with reasonable notice provided the replacement satisfies the same eligibility
requirements.
B Delivery Schedule and Obligations
The programme shall be delivered over 12 weeks in accordance with the schedule
annexed to this agreement. The provider shall supply qualified facilitators, learning
materials, and assessment administration; the commissioning organization shall supply
suitable venues or platform access, participant release time, and timely decisions on
nominations. Neither party shall be liable for delay caused by the other's failure to
perform its obligations.
Supporting records are presented in Table 5.
B.1 Scheduling, Attendance and Rescheduling
Sessions shall follow the agreed timetable, and the provider shall give reasonable notice
of any necessary change. Participants are expected to attend all scheduled sessions;
where absence exceeds the published threshold, the provider shall offer a catch-up
arrangement or record the module as incomplete. Rescheduling requested by the
commissioning organization is subject to facilitator availability and may attract a
reasonable administrative charge.
B.1.1 Attendance Records and Completion Criteria
The provider shall maintain attendance records for every session and reconcile them
against enrolment data before final results are issued. A participant is deemed to have
completed the programme only where attendance and assessment requirements are

both satisfied. Records of completion shall be issued within a reasonable period after the
final assessment and retained for audit purposes.
B.1.1.1 Minimum Attendance Threshold
Participants must attend at least the published proportion of scheduled sessions to
remain eligible for summative assessment. The provider shall publish this threshold
before enrolment and apply it uniformly. Absences supported by documented
exceptional circumstances may be considered under the provider's mitigation
procedure, with the outcome recorded and communicated to the participant.
B.1.1.2 Certification and Records
Certificates shall state the programme title, the participant's name, the completion date,
and the awarding body where applicable. The provider shall issue certificates only after
moderation is complete and all completion criteria are verified. Duplicate certificates
may be issued on written request, and the provider shall maintain a register linking each
certificate to its supporting assessment record.
B.1.2 Facilitator Qualifications and Substitution
Facilitators assigned to the programme must hold relevant subject expertise and
demonstrated instructional experience. The provider shall notify the commissioning
organization of any proposed substitution and confirm that the replacement meets
equivalent standards. Persistent facilitator underperformance identified through
participant feedback shall be addressed through the provider's performance
management process.
B.2 Fees, Invoicing and Payment Terms
Fees for the programme shall be invoiced in accordance with the payment schedule
agreed by the parties, with each invoice identifying the services delivered. The
commissioning organization shall pay undisputed invoices within the stated period and
may withhold disputed amounts pending resolution. The provider shall give written
notice of any fee adjustment before it takes effect.
Where a session is delivered remotely, the provider should confirm platform access,
recording consent, and participant connectivity in advance so that instructional time is
not lost to technical difficulties.
Attendance data should be reconciled against enrolment records before completion
decisions are finalized, since discrepancies discovered later are materially harder to
resolve fairly.
Any verbal instruction that changes scope, schedule, or assessment weighting should be
confirmed in writing within a short period so that the record reflects what was actually
agreed.
Participants who join late in the programme may require a documented induction
covering prior content, assessment expectations, and the attendance threshold
applicable to their enrolment.

The provider should retain facilitator credentials and continuing development records, as
these are commonly requested when the commissioning organization conducts a
supplier assurance review.
